--- change 1 (repo omnibase_spi, pull request #47) ---
feat(protocols): add typed-dynamic pattern for handler protocols [OMN-710] (#47)
* feat(protocols): add typed-dynamic pattern for handler protocols [OMN-710]

Replace `dict[str, Any]` with honest typed-dynamic primitives:

- Use `Mapping[str, JsonValue]` for open-ended payloads (metadata,
  properties, query parameters) - enforces JSON-safety
- Use TypedDict for known structures (ProducerMessage)
- Keep strongly-typed Core models for stable return shapes
- Add policy docstrings documenting opaque payload handling
- Document recommended constraints (max_keys=100, max_depth=5)

Design principle: "Typed at the boundary, flexible at the leaf"
- Stable invariants → strongly typed models
- Dynamic payloads → Mapping[str, JsonValue] with constraints
- Vendor-specific strictness

--- change 4 (repo omnibase_spi, pull request #307) ---
fix(OMN-17272): sync-only workflow_dispatch for release.yml main sync (#307)
A release has two halves with opposite retry properties: publishing is
irreversible, and moving main to the tag's commit is idempotent. Run
35304497808 published 0.23.4 and then failed at the sync, and the workflow
offered no way to retry only the repeatable half, because re-dispatching it
would have re-uploaded artifacts the index already holds.

Adds a default-false boolean sync_only input. When set, every publishing
step is skipped by an explicit if:, and only the app-token mint, the REST
main sync with force false, and the readback execute. Those three carry no
sync_only guard on purpose, and the readback stays terminal, so a sync-only
run that does not actually move the ref still fails

A release has two halves with opposite retry properties: publishing is
irreversible, and moving main to the tag's commit is idempotent. Run

offered no way to retry only the repeatable half, because re-dispatching it
would have re-uploaded artifacts the index already holds.

step is skipped by an explicit if:, and only the app-token mint, the REST
main sync with force false, and the readback execute. Those three carry no
sync_only guard on purpose, and the readback stays terminal, so a sync-only
run that does not actually move the ref still fails
